summary:
ALL FIFTEEN OF THE DECLARED DID-IT-FIRE NAMES ARE NOW LIVE, and eleven of them can reach the UNREACHABLE state.

WHAT I FOUND FIRST. The ten open_areas names were ALREADY BUILT in the current tree (Areas.counters carries data.holdout_overlap; Areas.gates carries the other nine, with data.holdout_seam as one gate per area) -- more than the previous fixer's report claims, so I verified each one live on both source arms rather than trusting the report, and changed none of them. The previous fixer's three named items are also present and correct: Stream.draws, Plan.counters (data.phase_resolved, data.protocol_named, data.phase_name_resolved) and rng_holdout's conditional seam_at/overlap/why.

WHAT WAS ACTUALLY MISSING was the whole draw_stream half: the Stream record had no `counters` and no `gates` field at all -- the module docstring's RECORD TYPES list named both, and neither existed -- so data.stream_draw, data.segment, data.contig_wrap, data.resample and data.phase_entered were text in a frozen docstring and nothing else. All five are now produced, exactly once each, on the returned Stream.

THE SPLIT, BY THE RULE THE Areas RECORD ALREADY STATES. Four are Gates because a configuration exists on which the mechanism CANNOT run (data.stream_draw, data.contig_wrap, data.resample, data.phase_entered); data.segment is a reading in counters because it describes the BYTES and stays true when the same Stream is handed back for a later epoch.

THE THIRD STATE IS REAL ON THE DEFAULT CONFIGURATION, which is the part worth the work: at DATA_RESAMPLE=0 (shipped) draw_stream returns the first draw's Stream for every later epoch, and `dataclasses.replace` copies every field -- so the naive version would have printed 'data.stream_draw: FIRED (40000 vs 40000)' for an epoch that drew nothing at all. data/api.py::_replay_gates re-states all four gates UNREACHABLE naming DATA_RESAMPLE=0, the epoch and the replayed stream_id, and leaves the counters alone.

COUNTS. 15 of 15 live. 11 carry a demonstrated UNREACHABLE arm (area_open, area_nested, area_path_refused, corpus_cap_trip, holdout_block, holdout_seam[label], val_cap_trip on DATA_SOURCE=synthetic; stream_draw, contig_wrap, resample, phase_entered on the replay / DATA_SEG_CONTIG=0 / DATA_RESAMPLE=0 arms). data.holdout_overlap carries the same three-way distinction inside its VALUE (float measured / None undefined / a sentence when there is no block), because the contract declares it a reading and not a gate. Three have NO unreachable arm by construction and each says so in its reason: data.area_label_collision and data.area_refused exit at startup so they read 0 in every Areas that exists, and data.segment is always evaluable. Every unreachable arm names the lever and the value that made it so.

PROVED, NOT ASSERTED. Every state above was produced by running a configuration and printing Gate.line(): eight configurations across both source arms (real eng; real eng + continual/01_rust nested with DATA_VAL_CAP=1000; real eng at DATA_CORPUS_CAP=20000/DATA_SEG_CONTIG=1 for the wrap; real eng at DATA_STREAM_BYTES=3 and 0 for the drift and the measured zero; DATA_RESAMPLE=1 over epochs 0 and 1; DATA_RESAMPLE=0 over epochs 0 and 1 for the replay; synthetic a,b at DATA_N_PROCESSES=2). No wire was spent -- src/data/api.py declares no d_ field and src/spine/assemble.py::COUPLINGS is untouched (git status shows one modified file). Measured on the build the suite runs, the ledger carries 19 rows against WIRE_BUDGET=25; the brief says 23 are spent, so one of the two numbers is stale and it is worth someone's look -- either way I added none. No RNG stream was minted, and draw_stream(epoch=0) twice in one process still raises RngError. The recorded end-to-end sequence reproduces its audited numbers byte for byte.

NOT DONE, and listed individually in `unfinished`: the five DID-IT-FIRE names on DATA.stream_state and DATA.restore_stream_state. They are outside the fifteen and both entry points are still P4 NotImplementedError stubs, so there is no record for them to land on.
